newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends weak on U.S. rate hike fears.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends weak on U.S. rate hike fears.

text.p: The Philippine peso ended weak at 26.344 on Friday from 26.333 in anticipation of a possible rise in U.S. interest rates, traders said.

If this happens, the hike will lower the peso's premium over the U.S. dollar and cause some foreign funds to leave the country, they said. On Thursday, Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan gave a warning that interest rates might be raised.
Traders also said the Central Bank might pursue a further cut in its overnight borrowing rate.
"The market is biddish on the dollar until the market is assured there would be no cut in interest rates," a dealer said.
Earlier in the day, the peso was pulled down to 26.345 due to arbitrage play for the coming weekend as banks sold dollars for same-day delivery and bought dollars for Monday-delivery.
Market volume rose to $191.1 million from $187.7 million.
